text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan agrees to hand the premiership over to his coalition partner Tansu Ciller in July on condition that they hold early elections.
- The high wheat subsidy price announced by the Islamist-led government aims to get votes from farmers. The government said it would buy wheat at $235 a tonne.
MILLIYET
- A "Poverty Summit" organsied by the United Nation and a Turkish education foundation group reveals that every one person in three in southeast Turkey is hungry.
- Turkish court fines Turkish celebrities who dodge taxes.
HURRIYET
- The far-right Grand Unity Party leader Muhsin Yazicioglu will be given deputy premiership when Ciller gets the premiership.
- Police arrest the first witness in the murder trial of "casino king" Omer Lutfu Topal.
YENI YUZYIL

- An Istanbul district mayor threw bags of gold into excited crowds during anniversary celebrations marking the conquest of Istanbul. But most of the bags were filled with almonds and only 50 of them contained gold.
RADIKAL
- Two coalition partners disagree on the date of early elections. The Islamist wing wants early elections to be held in September whereas the conservatives want them in March 1998.
- The Istanbul stock exchange, shocked by the prospect of an early election, closed down 36 points.
DUNYA
- Ciller said the minimum wage will be tax-free in 1998.
- The trade ministry is sueing three mass-circulation dailies over promotions.
ZAMAN
- The conquest of Istanbul was not an invasion but the end to the darkness of Byzantium.
CUMHURIYET
- An Islamist deputy, Sevket Yilmaz told a conference that the state religion in Turkey is Christianity and the parliament consists of pimps.
